r: Sanskrit work on **alankara (poetics)** praising **Prataparudra II**, by his court poet **Vidyanatha**
Historians identify the two; Agastya also wrote **Nalakirtikaumudi**, **Balabharata** and **Krishnacharita**
Author of **Madhura Vijayam** (Vijayanagara); hailed **Agastya** as her guru; the work also describes the hardship after the conquest
Another court poet of Prataparudra II

0.x: **"What Bana was to Harsha, Vidyanatha was to Prataparudradeva."**

r: **Ekamranatha** – Kakatiya traditions (Jaitugi–Ganapati marriage), Rudrama's Yadava victory
**Amir Khusrau** – Kafur's 1310 siege; Warangal fort **double-walled with a moat**; calls Prataparudra **Ravaddar Dev**
**Daughter of Ganapatideva** and **Kupama Devi**; Ganapati had **no son**, so she was raised as a son (**putrika**)
Under the male name **Rudradeva Maharaja**; sole rule from **1262**; ruled to **1289**

**First woman ruler of the Andhra region** (Rudramba); **second great woman ruler of medieval India after Razia Sultana**; among the **most prominent Kakatiya rulers**; inscriptions style her a **king**

1.x: **Recherla Prasaditya Nayaka** was Rudrama's general and protector (Kakatiya-rajya-sthapanacharya); her sons-in-law were **Mahadeva, Ellanadeva and Induluri Annaya**.

r: Defeated the Pandyas, the Eastern Gangas of Odisha and the Seunas of Devagiri
Title for her victory over the **rulers of Devagiri** (the Yadava **Mahadeva**, chased back to Devagiri)
Half-brothers **Harihara and Murari**, crushed with Recherla Prasaditya and others
Occupied by the Ganga **Narasimhadeva** (1262); regained in **1278** when **Poti Nayaka and Prolinayaka** beat Virabhanudeva
Killed fighting the Kayastha rebel **Ambadeva** (made head of Kadapa in 1272), with her general **Mallikarjuna Nayaka**
Set up by her servant **Puvvula Mummadi**; records her death
**Marco Polo**, the **Venetian (Italian)** traveller; work **Il Milione / The Travels**
In **Rudramadevi's** reign – he reached the Coromandel coast c. **1292–93**, "towards the end of her reign" (older books end her reign c. 1295)
She died in **Nov 1289** (Chandupatla inscription), so his "queen" account came just after her death, early in Prataparudra II's reign
Praised the queen's strict and just rule and the country's prosperity
Flourishing sea trade; port duties at Motupalli; merchants **not** heavily taxed
**Diamond** mines of the Golconda region; fine textiles
Hot climate; **rice** the only local grain
**Ulugh Khan** (Juna Khan, later **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**), under Sultan **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**
**1323** – the end of the Kakatiya kingdom; final siege of about **five months**; **Bobbareddi's** withdrawal weakened the defence

Andhra under **Malik Burhanuddin**; **Malik Maqbul** (the converted Brahmin Jagannatha Pandit) at Warangal
Survivors **Prolaya Nayaka, Racherla Singama, Prolaya Vema** led it → Musunuri and Reddi states
Southern disunity, weak cavalry, betrayal by chiefs, exhaustion from repeated raids (**not** a European sea blockade)
Grandson of Rudrama through **Mummadamma**; title **Kumara Rudradeva**; the last Kakatiya

Kingdom divided into **77 Nayankaras** held by military officers (**Nayakas**); each held a **fort**, kept troops and paid a **fixed tribute**; about **one-fourth** of the land
